input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: The sole governing-law clause selects Nova Scotia/Canadian law with Nova Scotia courts. That is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), so it fails both the preferred and fallback positions on the material term of governing law and forum. There is no arbitration provision, so this is not walk-away territory, but the jurisdiction words must change. We propose the preferred position — New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County — editing only the jurisdiction and forum wording and leaving the rest of the clause intact.

proposal.summary: Change governing law from Nova Scotia to New York with exclusive New York County courts
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have moved governing law and venue from Nova Scotia to New York, with exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, consistent with our standard position. If helpful, we can accept Delaware, California, or England and Wales (with the courts of London) as an alternative.

ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
